text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Prime minister Wim Kok denies deal between cabinet and coalition parties Labour PvdA and D66 on route for high-speed rail link (HSL). (p1)
- Reports of hidden copper mountain in Rotterdam Port are based on flawed data, national statistics office CBS says. (p1)
- D.I.Y. sector in the Netherlands achieves higher turnover with fewer shops. (p3)
- Half the Dutch population will have access to Internet via TV cable network in three years' time, according to report by four major cable operators. (p3)
- Philips Electronics chief Cor Boonstra says consumer electronics sector should step up marketing drive and increase cooperation between manufacturers and sales. (p3)
- Car maker NedCar to double production to 300,000 cars annually over next three years. (p3)
- Publisher Frank Kloppert merges its four publishing units into one new organisation named Readers House. (p3)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Philips Electronics plans to shed stakes in cable TV networks, worth about Dfl 1.2 bn. (p1)
- Economic affairs ministry bans collective sale of rights for first division soccer matches by football association KNVB. (p1)
- Retailer Ahold's supermarket unit Albert Heijn forces ABN Amro bank to accept payments by Postbank customers using AH customer card with ABN Amro chip. (p2)
- Dutch aviation and space institute NIVR to set up Dutch company to take part in Euro Airbus project. (p2)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Traffic minister does not give in to parliamentary pressure to abandon plans for widening Amsterdam-Utrecht trunk road in favour of rail-tunnel near Amsterdam. (p7)
- Automation firm Triple P takes over rival Mediasystemen.
- Investment group Robeco eyeing real estate portfolio of Scottish Amicable Investment Managers. (p39)
- Broker AOT upgrades full year profit forecast to more than four guilders per share from three guilders per share. (p41)
TROUW
- Industrial company Begemann's board chairman A. Deleye under investigation in Belgian probe into subsidy irregularities. (p1)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Economic affairs ministry tried to withhold information during government's audit office inquiry into government support for Fokker, NedCar and DAF. (p1)
- Philips to open head offices in North and South America in order to spread its chief tasks, now coordinated from Eindhoven. (p13) --Amsterdam newsdesk +31-20-504-5000
